| 0017 | Adversarial review gives the coverage layer a mechanism | accepted |
| 0018 | The hook checks the commit, not the working tree | accepted |
| 0019 | Immutable bodies may gain lines, never lose them | accepted |
| 0020 | Citations are checked wherever they are read, and vendored text names its own repo | accepted |
| 0021 | The checked scope is one exported list, and no rule reads outside it | accepted |
| 0022 | Mutation checking is a curated list in a wired script, and measures durability rather than correctness | amended |
| 0023 | Slash commands are vendored per repo, and an update overwrites only what the repo has not touched | accepted |
| 0024 | The quality bar ships with the method, vendored into the repo, and tests derive from the spec rather than from the code | amended |
| 0025 | The established solution is the default; a hand-rolled replacement is argued in writing with a named cost and a measured build | accepted |
| 0026 | The changelog is generated from tags, and release engineering is not enforced on the repos the method installs into | accepted |
| 0027 | The Claude Code lifecycle hook is a fast path over the git hook, never an invariant's only enforcement | accepted |
